newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope to leave hospital on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Pope to leave hospital on Tuesday.

text.p: The Vatican said on Monday that Pope John Paul would leave hospital on Tuesday, a week after surgery to remove his appendix.
A Vatican statement said the 76-year-old Pope would return to his quarters at the Vatican for further convalescence. It said his post-operative recovery was continuing in a satisfactory manner.
The statement said doctors at Rome's Gemelli hospital would remove his stitches on Tuesday morning and that the Pope would leave hospital at midday.

"He will return to the Vatican where he will spend a period of convalescence and rest according to his doctors' orders," the Vatican said. It added that the Pope would gradually resume his daily activities.

The Pope made his first public appearance since surgery on Sunday. He spoke for five minutes from the window of his hospital room, thanking doctors and nurses for their care and joking that the hospital had become the "third Vatican" after Saint Peter's basilica and the papal summer residence near Rome.
Doctors have said the surgery was a success and confirmed there had been no recurrence of a colon tumor removed in 1992.
